source.title: Pharmacodynamics of Cefazolin in the Presence of Normal and Impaired Renal Function
source.design: single-dose intramuscular cefazolin study across renal function, with a three-volunteer within-subject probenecid re-exposure

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary study methods, central pharmacokinetic results, all Table 2 clearance rows, renal-excretion findings, safety observations, conclusions, funding, and source-integrity limitations were atomized. atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to characterize cefazolin excretion across degrees of renal failure, assess the effect of probenecid, and develop a practical guide for maintaining acceptable serum concentrations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study was undertaken to determine the rate of excretion of cefazolin in patients with varying degrees of renal failure, to evaluate the effect of probenecid, and to develop a simple guide for administration of the drug.

atoms.canonical_statement: The healthy-volunteer cohort comprised five informed volunteers without renal, hepatic, or infectious disease and without drug exposure during the preceding 2 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Five informed volunteers with no evidence of renal, hepatic, or infectious disease and who had received no drugs during the preceding 2 weeks

population.label: Healthy volunteers
inclusion_criteria: No drugs during the preceding 2 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: The renal-failure cohort was described as nine informed patients with renal failure of diverse etiologies, no concurrent infection or antibiotic therapy, and normal listed hepatic and related laboratory tests.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nine patients with varying degrees of renal failure of diverse etiologies gave informed consent and received 500 mg of cefazolin intramuscularly.

population.label: Patients with renal failure
inclusion_criteria: No evidence of concurrent infection or antibiotic therapy
Normal listed bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, amylase, LDH, SGOT, and SGPT values

atoms.canonical_statement: Healthy volunteers were excluded by evidence of renal, hepatic, or infectious disease or by drug use within the preceding 2 weeks.

population.label: Healthy-volunteer eligibility
inclusion_criteria: No renal, hepatic, or infectious disease
No drug use during preceding 2 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Renal-failure patients were required to have no concurrent infection or antibiotic therapy and normal values for the listed hepatic and related laboratory tests.

population.label: Renal-failure patient eligibility
inclusion_criteria: Normal bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, amylase, LDH, SGOT, SGPT

atoms.canonical_statement: All main-study administrations used a single 500 mg intramuscular cefazolin dose.
Three healthy volunteers received probenecid 500 mg orally every 6 hours for four doses; cefazolin 500 mg intramuscularly was given 1 hour after the first probenecid dose.

exposures.details: given 1 hour after first probenecid dose

atoms.canonical_statement: Serum and urine cefazolin concentrations were measured by a modified Bacillus subtilis agar-diffusion assay, using human-serum standards for serum samples and water standards for urine samples.

source_anchor.paragraph: Cefazolin assay in serum and urine
source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Standards of cefazolin were prepared by serial dilution in human serum for use in assaying the serum samples and in water for assaying urine specimens.

atoms.canonical_statement: Assay samples were run in triplicate, and serum concentrations below 5 micrograms per milliliter were excluded because they could not be measured accurately.

source_anchor.paragraph: Cefazolin assay in serum and urine
source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Serum levels of less than 5 pg/ml could not be accurately determined and were excluded.

atoms.canonical_statement: Selected serum assay results were cross-checked by parallel broth tube-dilution testing with Staphylococcus aureus.

source_anchor.paragraph: Cefazolin assay in serum and urine

atoms.canonical_statement: Serum cefazolin half-life was derived from the least-squares slope of the descending portion of semilogarithmic serum concentration-time curves.

outcome.definition: Derived from least-squares approximation of the descending semilog serum concentration-time curve

atoms.canonical_statement: Renal cefazolin clearance in normal volunteers was calculated from the 2- to 4-hour urine collection and the geometric mean of serum concentrations at the start and end of that interval.

outcome.definition: Urine volume × urine level divided by 120 minutes and geometric mean serum level

atoms.canonical_statement: All reported clearances were corrected to a body surface area of 1.73 square meters.
Across the study observations, creatinine clearance ranged from 0 to 144 mL/min/1.73 m2 and the fixed 500 mg dose corresponded to 5.80 to 9.78 mg/kg.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: the 500-mg injection yielded cefazolin doses ranging from 5.80 to 9.78 mg/kg

atoms.canonical_statement: In subjects with creatinine clearance above 100 mL/min, peak serum cefazolin concentrations occurred 30 to 60 minutes after injection and ranged from 44 to 70 micrograms per milliliter.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Peak serum levels in the normal subjects ... occurred between 30 and 60 min ... and ranged from 44.0 to 70.0 pg/ml.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the normal subjects, serum cefazolin half-life ranged from 1.37 to 1.96 hours with a reported mean of 1.60 hours.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: serum half-life ... ranged from 1.37 to 1.96 h with a mean half-life of 1.60 h

atoms.canonical_statement: Among patients with renal impairment, a serum half-life of 4.83 hours was associated with creatinine clearance of about 47 mL/min, while an anuric observation had a half-life of 69.2 hours.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: ranged from 4.83 h associated with a creatinine clearance of 47.2 ml/min to 69.2 h in an anuric patient

atoms.canonical_statement: The abstract reported an approximately 42-hour serum half-life in anephric patients.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: The serum half-life in anephric patients was about 42 h.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the three healthy volunteers retested with probenecid, cefazolin serum half-life was reported to increase by about 20% to 40% relative to cefazolin alone.

source_anchor.paragraph: Effect of probenecid on excretion of cefazolin

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Probenecid prolonged the serum half-life from 20 to 40% over its values in the same subjects

atoms.canonical_statement: With probenecid, peak serum cefazolin concentrations ranged from 47.0 to 82.5 micrograms per milliliter and were reported as 7% to 33% higher than without probenecid.

source_anchor.paragraph: Effect of probenecid on excretion of cefazolin

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Peak serum levels ranged from 47.0 to 82.5 ug/ml, representing an increase of from 7 to 33%.

atoms.canonical_statement: Creatinine clearances measured during probenecid administration were lower than baseline values in the same subjects.

atoms.canonical_statement: Fractional cefazolin clearance increased as mean serum cefazolin concentration increased during the 2-hour collection period.
In normal subjects, peak serum cefazolin concentration was strongly related to weight-adjusted dose, with a reported multiple correlation coefficient of 0.99.

atoms.canonical_statement: Normal volunteers and patients with renal impairment reported relatively little injection-site discomfort and no local drug reaction.
Where tested, the investigators attributed no impairment of renal, hematological, or hepatic function to the single cefazolin dose.
The authors concluded that the kidney is the major route of cefazolin excretion in humans.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Thus, the kidney represents the major pathway for excretion of cefazolin in the human.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that cefazolin is handled primarily by glomerular filtration with a smaller component of renal tubular secretion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The drug is handled primarily by glomerular filtration with a smaller component of renal tubular secretion.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors proposed that serum cefazolin half-life can be approximated from creatinine clearance across renal function.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For practical purposes the serum half-life of the drug correlates well with creatinine clearance.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors suggested that biliary excretion is minor in normal renal function but may become more important in renal failure.

The participant accounting is internally inconsistent: the abstract states that 12 subjects were studied, the methods describe five healthy volunteers plus nine renal-failure patients, and Table 1 contains 14 non-probenecid observation rows with C.L. listed twice at different creatinine clearances.
The study used a single 500 mg intramuscular dose in a small sample and did not evaluate repeated-dose accumulation or clinical treatment outcomes.
The study reports no demographic description sufficient to assess age, sex, body-size distribution, or other covariates beyond renal function and the listed screening laboratories.
Eli Lilly Company supported the project and supplied cefazolin injectable material and laboratory standards.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We are indebted to the Eli Lilly Company for their support of this project and for supplying cefazolin injectable and laboratory standards.
